name: prompt-bar
description:
The one place you talk to the system — text or voice — pinned to the bottom of the app. It is a single unit because it is a single interface: the app deliberately has ONE input, and a second way to ask for something is a second place for the answer to arrive.

The growing textarea is the part everyone rebuilds and few get right. It has to grow with the content up to a cap and then scroll, and it has to do that without the page jumping — which means the bar is anchored to the bottom and grows upward, not a block in the flow that pushes everything down as you type.

base.$description:
Anchored to the bottom and growing UPWARD. A composer in the normal flow pushes the conversation down as it grows, which moves the thing you are replying to while you type.

CONTAINER. This unit establishes an inline-size container named after itself, so anything inside it can respond to the width of THIS BOX rather than to the width of the window. That is the difference that matters for a design system: a composite dropped into a 320px sidebar and the same composite on a 320px phone are the same situation, and a viewport query calls them different ones. The library carries no viewport media query anywhere for exactly this reason — the only `@media` in it is `prefers-reduced-motion`, which is a person's setting and not a size.

shell.$description:
A rounded rectangle on a raised ground, with the shadow doing the lifting and no border at all.

Two wrong answers preceded this one. First `radius-xl` with a 1px grey hairline, which read as a search box. Then a 2px marine edge copied from the app's composer — correct to the source and wrong here: at this radius and this scale the marine line reads as a thin blue hairline rather than as an edge, and it competes with the send button that is already the marine thing on the bar. `gate-card` earns that edge because a gate is a card you must answer; a prompt is a place you type, and the shadow is enough to say it is raised.

input.$description: Grows to a cap, then scrolls. `field-sizing: content` does it natively where supported; the `max-block-size` is the cap, and without one a pasted essay takes the whole screen. `resize: none` because the grab handle contradicts the automatic growth.

hint.$description: What the system is doing, or what it just heard. Above the bar, not inside it — text inside the shell competes with what you are typing.

mode.$description: Typing or talking. The same bar — a second component for voice would be a second place for the answer to arrive.

listening.$description: Recording. The shell carries the state so the whole bar reads as live, and the hint above says what was heard so far — a listening indicator with no transcript is a microphone you have to trust blindly.

docked.$description: Fixed to the bottom of the viewport for a full-screen surface.

reducedMotion.$description: The listening ring stops pulsing but stays visible — it is the only signal that the microphone is open.

a11y.note: The textarea carries its own label; a placeholder is not one, and it disappears the moment someone types. Enter submits and Shift+Enter makes a newline, which has to be stated in the hint because it is not discoverable. Voice needs a visible transcript: an indicator alone asks the user to trust an open microphone with no way to check what it heard. `aria-busy` while a reply is in flight, and the reply itself lands in a live region — not here.
